questions.question: 1. What is the key characteristic of 'flat fading'?

answers.a: It affects only the high-frequency parts of a signal.
answers.b: It affects only the low-frequency parts of a signal.
answers.c: It affects all frequency components of the signal in a similar way.
answers.d: It is a signal gain, not a loss.

answers.a: The probability that the system is powered down for maintenance.
answers.b: The probability that the received signal quality falls below a usable threshold.
answers.c: The likelihood that a user moves out of the cell's coverage area.
answers.d: The probability that a new call is successfully connected.

questions.question: 3. What does the 'Level Crossing Rate' (LCR) measure?

answers.a: How often the signal strength crosses a specific level.
answers.b: The average speed of the mobile user.
answers.c: The total number of users in a cell.
answers.d: The average time a signal stays in a faded state.

answers.a: The average time it takes to connect a call.
answers.b: The average time the signal stays below a specific level once it drops.
answers.c: The frequency at which the signal fades the most.
answers.d: The total duration of the entire communication.

questions.question: 5. What does the diversity technique 'Selection Combining' (SC) do?

answers.a: It combines all received signals by adding them together.
answers.b: It averages the quality of all received signals.
answers.c: It discards all signals and waits for a better one.
answers.d: It selects the single best signal from multiple received paths.

questions.question: 6. How does 'Maximal-Ratio Combining' (MRC) improve the signal?

answers.a: It selects only the signal with the lowest noise.
answers.b: It inverts the phase of bad signals to cancel them out.
answers.c: It intelligently combines all signals, giving more weight to the stronger ones.
answers.d: It only uses the two strongest signals and discards the rest.

questions.question: 7. How does the performance of MRC generally compare to Selection Combining (SC) in a SISO system?

answers.a: MRC provides a better improvement in signal quality.
answers.b: SC provides a better improvement in signal quality.
answers.c: They both provide the exact same level of improvement.
answers.d: SC is better for LCR, but MRC is better for ADF.

questions.question: 8. What is the primary goal of using diversity combining (SC or MRC) in a fading environment?

answers.a: To increase the Level Crossing Rate.
answers.b: To increase the Average Fade Duration.

questions.question: 9. A system is described as 'SISO'. What does this mean?

answers.a: It has multiple transmit and multiple receive antennas.
answers.b: It has multiple transmit and a single receive antenna.
answers.c: It has a single transmit and a single receive antenna.
answers.d: It has a single transmit and multiple receive antennas.

questions.question: 10. If a diversity scheme is working well, what change would you expect in the LCR and ADF?

answers.a: Both LCR and ADF would increase.
answers.b: LCR would increase, but ADF would decrease.
answers.c: Both LCR and ADF would decrease.
answers.d: LCR would decrease, but ADF would increase.
